problems.what: Give the size of a force/pressure acting in a clause ('pushes back with about 15 mmHg')
problems.workaround: Used SPAN (extent) rather than WITH; unsure which role is intended.

problems.what: SELF in a CAUSE/FOR block referring to the outer clause's THEME ('they do not pass because they are too big')

problems.what: Correct a common misconception that is not an earlier sentence: REBUT without a label points at the previous sentence, and there is no way to target 'what the reader is presumed to think' explicitly
problems.workaround: CLAIM EMPHASIS NOT true THEME idea KIND common KIND { ... } with no REBUT relation.

problems.what: Nested 'of' chains (cell of the wall of the tubule; wall of the descending limb) since every modifier attaches to the head
problems.workaround: Bound many handles (11 in total) and bracketed each inner phrase; in one place split into separate role phrases (AGENT cell OF duct ... AT wall OF duct).

problems.what: A gradient 'rising from 300 at the top to 1200 at the bottom'
problems.workaround: Two EQUAL clauses joined with ANDC, each with a bracketed AT top/bottom REL phrase, since FROM/TO each needing its own AT was ambiguous.

problems.what: Three-item step list mixing act roots, a spare word and a derived word after NOTE
problems.workaround: 3 step NOTE ( filter AND SPARE AND absorb.opp ); unsure a bare spare word is accepted as a phrase head in a joined list.

problems.what: antigen, antibody, helper T cell, B cell, plasma cell, memory cell, dendritic/antigen-presenting cell, germinal centre, affinity: core technical terms with no roots
problems.workaround: Used up nine spare words with DEFINE sentences (e.g. antigen = thing that the immune system recognises; dendritic cell = cell HAVING MANY branch that shows antigen to other cells). These took 9 of the 35 sentences, which left less room for content.

problems.what: lymph node
problems.workaround: node KIND loan ~lymph (차러뻐머). The loan is clumsy and the reader may not recognise it.

problems.what: mutation / somatic hypermutation; base pair / nucleotide
problems.workaround: 'change KIND random' of 'gene KIND antibody'. For the rate (about 1 in 1000 base pairs per division) I wrote 'around 1 place OF gene PER 1000 place'. 'place' for base pair is vague.

problems.workaround: receptor = antibody KIND {on REL surface REL B cell}; cytokine = message KIND protein; costimulation = adhesion OF CD80 protein TO CD28 protein; bone marrow = middle REL bone; vaccination = giving OF vaccine. I left out the T cell receptor.

problems.what: Technical terms 'affinity maturation' and 'class switching' as recognised English terms
problems.workaround: Used DEFINE ( phrase ) BE «affinity maturation». The rule sheet presents this form as giving a code identifier, so using it to gloss a scientific term stretches it.

problems.what: Time span over which a comparison holds ('over several weeks affinity becomes 10-1000 times higher')
problems.workaround: SPAN after a MORE/EQUAL comparison means the size of the difference, so I could not use SPAN for duration there. I wrote WHEN ( end REL several week ) instead.

problems.what: 'X days after vaccination': the rule sheet only shows 'ago REL 2 day' and has no 'N days after event' pattern
problems.workaround: WHEN ( after.opp-of-before REL ( giving OF vaccine ) ) SPAN ( 5 UPTO 7 day ). It is unclear whether SPAN here reads as the offset or as a duration.

problems.what: A rate inside a phrase: '1 per 1000' as an extent
problems.workaround: Put PER at clause level: '... THEME ( around 1 place OF gene ) PER ( 1000 place )'. It works but reads indirectly.

problems.what: 'becomes N times as large' right after a relation with labels (a number after a relation is read as a label)
problems.workaround: Put BEGIN (저) between the labels and the number, e.g. 'RESULT 18 19 20 BEGIN 10 UPTO 1000 EQUAL big ...'.

problems.what: 'B cell survives selection' / programmed cell death (apoptosis)
problems.workaround: 'STILL alive THEME B' and plain 'die' for cells that bind weakly.

problems.what: 35-sentence cap together with the definition overhead
problems.workaround: Dropped details I wanted to include: the rarity of matching T cells (about 1 in 10^5), the 10^6-fold higher mutation rate, which antibody parts change in class switching, and T follicular helper cells.

problems.what: cell membrane
problems.workaround: Spare 사붕 defined as 'thin sheet that covers the cell' (띠글 라 이펍안 라 { 프멀 사 어 새 조닉 })

problems.what: membrane potential / voltage (electrical potential difference)
problems.workaround: Spare 거뭄 defined as 'inequality of charge between inside of cell and outside of cell'; magnitudes given with «mV»

problems.what: axon, action potential, neuromuscular junction, acetylcholine, receptor, sarcoplasmic reticulum, actin, myosin, myosin head (cross-bridge), troponin/tropomyosin
problems.workaround: Ten spare words were defined by description (e.g. actin = thin thread that is part of muscle; troponin = protein that covers the place on actin). The real names (acetylcholine, troponin, tropomyosin, T-tubule, sarcomere) do not appear because the rules give no clear way to attach a technical name to a spare word

problems.what: ion, sodium, potassium, calcium, ADP, inorganic phosphate

problems.what: Saying 'after 1 ms' or 'within 1 ms' relative to an event
problems.workaround: Used SPAN with about 1 «ms» in front of the predicate. The 'after REL x' (before.opp) pattern seemed ambiguous for a duration

problems.what: SELF inside a nested non-KIND block within a KIND block (for a receptor defined as 'channel that opens when it catches ACh')
problems.workaround: Rewrote it as one KIND block with two clauses joined by ANDC, so that SELF clearly refers to the channel

problems.what: The task asks for 20-35 sentences, but the vocabulary forced 12 DEFINE sentences for spare words

problems.workaround: Power stroke = 'head turns and pulls actin toward middle of muscle unit about 10 nm'. Hydrolysis = 'head breaks ATP to (ADP and Pi)'. Re-cocking = 'head turns again to old position'

problems.what: Whether a number may directly precede a « » notation head as a count (3 «Na+», 1 «ATP»)
problems.workaround: Wrote it that way, by analogy with '2 parameter', without being sure it is allowed

problems.what: haemoglobin, kidney, Bohr (no roots)
problems.workaround: Letter-table loans (hemoglobin, kidney, bohr) and a handle for haemoglobin. The loans are opaque strings; kidney as a loan is especially unreadable.

problems.what: Technical terms: saturation, affinity, partial pressure, ion, bicarbonate, enzyme, plasma, alveolus, erythropoietin, cooperative binding
problems.workaround: Defined two spares (saturation = percent of A's places holding oxygen; affinity = strength of joining A and oxygen); wrote 'pressure of oxygen' for partial pressure (the 'partial' is lost); 'particle «H+»' for ion; 'protein «carbonic anhydrase»' for enzyme; 'liquid of blood' for plasma; 'lung' for alveoli; put «EPO», «cooperative binding», «P50» in notation.

problems.what: bind / release (chemical binding), oxygenated / deoxygenated
problems.workaround: join (므듭) for bind, absorb.opp for release, relative clauses 'A that holds / does not hold / has released oxygen' for oxy/deoxy forms.

problems.what: Use a « » notation item (H+, CO2, 2,3-BPG, pH) as a noun phrase in prose
problems.workaround: The sheet only shows « » after a root or after NAME, so I always prefixed a class root: gas «CO2», particle «H+», molecule «2,3-BPG», value «pH». Unsure whether bare « » after a role particle is legal.

problems.what: State a measured quantity: 'X is about 100 mmHg', 'carries 1.34 mL of oxygen'
problems.workaround: Used EQUAL THEME x THAN AROUND 100 «mmHg» for values and THEME oxygen SPAN AROUND 1.34 «mL» for amounts. Not clear whether number+«unit» can be a phrase head taking KIND/OF ('1.34 mL of oxygen'), nor whether AROUND may precede the multiplier in 'AROUND 240 EQUAL strong'.

problems.what: Comparative manner on an act: 'breathes faster', 'changes fast'
problems.workaround: KIND after the predicate with a bracket: breathe KIND ( MORE fast ). The sheet says KIND after a predicate is manner but gives no example, and none with a degree word.

problems.what: Bare comparison with a number in prose: 'P is above 70 mmHg', 'P is below 10 mmHg'
problems.workaround: MORE big THEME P THAN 70 «mmHg» / MORE big.opp ... Only EQUAL is shown as a standalone prose predicate; MORE/LESS alone appear only in logic form, and ABOVE/BELOW are number modifiers not predicates.

problems.what: Counterfactual conditional ('if there were no BPG, haemoglobin would barely release oxygen')
problems.workaround: Put UNREAL inside both blocks of IF. The sheet does not say where UNREAL goes relative to IF.

problems.what: Name a phenomenon described by an earlier sentence ('this is called the Bohr effect') and name a value ('this value is called P50')
problems.workaround: name REL STEP 17 THEME ( affect.made KIND NAME bohr ) and name REL THIS value OF P THEME NAME «P50». Unsure whether STEP n can be the REL term of a root and whether DEFINE can take a « » term in prose, so I avoided DEFINE «P50» BE ....

problems.what: Role phrases inside a noun phrase and nested modifiers ('the count of red cells', 'state T with weak affinity', 'strength of the binding of CO')
problems.workaround: Heavy bracketing, e.g. ( ( state «T» HAVING ( affinity KIND strong.opp ) ) AND ( state «R» HAVING ( affinity KIND strong ) ) ). Easy to get wrong because every modifier attaches to the head.

problems.what: Range 'between 20 and 40 mmHg' and 'from pH 7.4 to 7.2'
problems.workaround: between REL ( 20 «mmHg» AND 40 «mmHg» ) THEME P; unclear whether UPTO may be used with units, so I avoided it and dropped the pH-shift numeric example.

problems.what: Chemical equation CO2 + H2O -> H+ + HCO3-
problems.workaround: change KIND fast AGENT enzyme THEME ( gas «CO2» AND water ) TO ( particle «H+» AND particle «HCO3-» ); no reaction arrow or 'react to form' construction, and the reversibility is not expressed.

problems.what: 'Shift the curve to the left/right'

problems.what: Task asks for 20-35 sentences; with strict one-clause statements the content needed heavy clause chaining with ANDC to fit
problems.workaround: Wrote exactly 35 long sentences, dropping the Haldane effect, fetal haemoglobin, the numeric Bohr shift and CO treatment; no headings were used since it is unclear whether HEAD lines count as sentences.

problems.what: Mixing ANDC and BUT in one sentence ('..., and so ..., but ...')
problems.workaround: Rule says mixed joiners need brackets but does not show how to bracket clauses (only phrases), so I replaced BUT with ANDC CONTRAST / ANDC ADD.

problems.what: 'orbital' (atomic/molecular orbital), the central term of the task
problems.workaround: Defined spare 사붕 as 'wave function that describes the state of 1 electron'; atomic vs molecular orbital written as 사붕 OF atom / 사붕 OF molecule, which forces brackets whenever it is itself a modifier

problems.what: 'chemical bond' as a thing (word list has connect/join acts only), and 'bonding' / 'antibonding' orbital
problems.workaround: Defined spare 모민 = chemical connection joining 2 atoms; defined spare 거뭄 = bonding orbital and used 거뭄+opp suffix for antibonding without a separate definition (unclear whether the opp of a defined spare is understood as 'antibonding')

problems.what: 'paramagnetic' / 'diamagnetic', 'magnetic field', 'magnetic moment', 'attract' and 'repel'

problems.what: electron 'spin' (turn/rotation would be misleading)
problems.workaround: Loan 허뽀터 (spin), undefined

problems.what: 'unpaired' / 'paired' electron; 'valence' electrons; 'shell'; 'degenerate' orbitals; 'node' of a wave function (the list's node is a network node)
problems.workaround: 'electron KIND alone' for unpaired; 'all electrons belong to pairs' for paired; dropped valence/shell and counted all 16 electrons incl. 1s; 'orbital HAVING (SAME energy)' for degenerate; dropped the nodal-plane description of antibonding orbitals

problems.what: 'bond order', 'bond length', 'bond energy (dissociation energy)', 'double bond'

problems.what: Define a spare word as a quality (so that 'paramagnetic THEME O2' works as a predicate). The sheet says a spare may be a thing, act or quality but shows only a thing definition
problems.workaround: Defined it as a property (thing) and wrote 'have AGENT molecule THEME paramagnetism'

problems.what: Whether a count expression inside logic may take a bracketed role phrase as its argument: count FIRST ( electron AT bonding-orbital )
problems.workaround: Wrote exactly that, by analogy with the '( evidence ABOUT fact )' convention; not sure the converter accepts it inside a DEFINE expression

problems.what: Whether a bare « » name or a root+«name» is the right way to refer to a specific molecule or orbital as a participant (e.g. O2, the π*2p orbital)
problems.workaround: Always wrote root + notation: 'molecule «O2»', 'orbital «π*2p»'; and put the whole electron configuration in one « » string after NOTE

problems.what: 'before X happens' with a clause: REL is a linker and the sheet only lets role particles take a { } block, so 'before REL { pairs form }' is not covered
problems.workaround: Used a joined clause with a relation: 'ANDC SEQUENCE pairs begin to exist'

problems.what: Manner adverb on a predicate with its own degree ('pull more strongly'); KIND-after-predicate manner cannot sit after the participants and degree+quality cannot precede the predicate

problems.what: Nested genitives such as 'the energy of the bonding orbital of the atom' or 'the bond order of the O2 molecule'; because every modifier attaches to the head, almost every such phrase needs ( ) and the text becomes bracket-heavy
problems.workaround: Bracketed every inner phrase; repeated 'molecule «O2»' in full instead of a pronoun-like reference

problems.what: State a quantity with a unit as a value: 'the bond length is 121 pm' and a table of three molecules with order, length, energy
problems.workaround: Repeated 'EQUAL THEME ( length OF bond ) THAN 121 «pm»' clause by clause joined with ANDC, giving very long sentences; no table or list construction

problems.what: State the Aufbau principle ('orbitals are filled in order of increasing energy')
problems.workaround: 'A new electron dwells at the orbital that is available and whose energy is least high'

problems.what: Point REBUT at a misconception held by the reader rather than at an earlier sentence of mine

problems.what: Task asks 20-35 sentences; definitions of spares (5 sentences) eat into the budget, so I dropped the s-p mixing/orbital ordering remark, the bond-energy definition, and the liquid-oxygen temperature
problems.workaround: Kept 35 numbered sentences plus a heading; merged data for O2/F2 and for O2+/O2- into single long sentences

problems.what: Core terms of the topic: substrate, nucleophile, leaving group, carbocation, transition state, mirror image, protic solvent, aprotic solvent, chemical bond
problems.workaround: Defined 9 spare words with DEFINE sentences (사붕, 모민, 거뭄, 포법, 띠밧, 서작, 두덜, 베릉, 호쿳). Nine definition sentences took up much of the 20-35 sentence budget, so the text ended up with 36 numbered sentences.

problems.workaround: Defined spare 호쿳 = join.made KIND {pair of electrons joins 2 atoms}. For 'hydrogen bond', which is not an electron-pair bond, I had to fall back on 므듭엄 라 오망 (join.made KIND hydrogen), so two different words now cover one English term.

problems.what: 'polar' (solvent)

problems.what: 'concentration'
problems.workaround: Used dense.ness (루눌음).

problems.what: 'reaction rate' / 'rate law' / 'reaction order'

problems.what: 'chiral', 'stereocentre', 'inversion of configuration', 'racemic mixture', and 'configuration' in the chemical sense

problems.what: 'intermediate', 'partial bond', 'backside attack', 'steric hindrance', 'hyperconjugation/inductive donation', 'solvation', 'ion', 'anion', 'elimination (E1/E2)', 'molecularity'

problems.what: Wanted 'A and B, but C' within one sentence (for example, racemic mixture BUT slight excess of the inverted form due to ion pairs)
problems.workaround: Mixing ANDC and BUT at one level needs brackets, which made the sentence very long. I dropped the ion-pair point to save sentences.

problems.what: Writing angle values such as 120° and 180° as a property ('flat with 120° angles')
problems.workaround: Used 'all angles at the carbon of the carbocation are EQUAL THAN 120 «°»'. For 180° I just said Nu, C and the leaving group lie on the same line.

problems.what: Scope of a fronted role phrase ('in the transition state of B') over the later ANDC-joined clauses
problems.workaround: Fronted AT (TS of B) once and joined the next clauses with ANDC. It is unclear whether the AT phrase carries over to them.

problems.what: Statements of class membership ('I- is a strong nucleophile', 'acetone is an aprotic solvent')
problems.workaround: Used the class phrase as the predicate (모민 라 키틀 새 «I-»), following the 'all dogs are animals' pattern. It works but reads stiffly.

problems.what: Setting up a worked case with a chiral carbon and naming its two mirror forms
problems.workaround: Used a STORY sentence to bind handles 혹, 박 and 닥, then cited it from DERIVED sentences. A scenario mixed with recalled facts sits awkwardly with the evidence system.

problems.workaround: Defined five spare words (사붕 spin, 모민 magnetic field, 포법 spectrum, 거뭄 chemical shift, 누룰 integral) with DEFINE sentences; this cost 5 of the 35 allowed sentences and the definitions are loose paraphrases (e.g. magnetic field = 'space in which the force of a magnet exists').

problems.what: 'proportional to' (energy gap proportional to field strength; peak area proportional to number of protons)
problems.workaround: Used the 'the more..., the more...' IF construction for the gap, and 'ratio of integrals equals ratio of proton counts' for integration. Strict linear proportionality is lost in the first case.

problems.what: 'resonance', 'peak', 'multiplet/triplet/quartet', 'coupling constant', 'shielding/deshielding', 'electronegative', 'chemical exchange', 'bond' (chemical)
problems.workaround: signal (메근) for peak; 'splits into 3 lines' for triplet; 'frequency gap between 2 neighbouring lines' for J; 'electrons decrease the field strength at the proton' for shielding; 'atom that strongly takes electrons' for electronegative; 'the proton moves fast between several molecules' for exchange; connect.made for bond. problems.what: Use a computed expression as a count before a noun: '(n+1) lines'. The sheet only says a handle may stand as a count, and that bracketed expressions are allowed as ORD range ends.

problems.what: Introduce a free variable n for a general rule ('a proton with n neighbours'). Handles must be bound with NAMED, but there is nothing to name before the count exists.
problems.workaround: Wrapped the rule in 'EACH N IN ALL integer KIND ( NOT negative )' so that EACH binds the handle; heavy for a simple rule, and I am unsure NOT inside a KIND bracket on a derived .opp word reads as 'non-negative'.

problems.what: Attach a quantity with a unit to a noun: 'a field of 9.4 T', 'signal at 1.2 ppm', 'shift expressed in ppm'. The sheet shows number+unit only after role particles like SPAN.

problems.what: State what a signal comes from ('signal X is produced by a CH3 group attached to a CH2 group') and name chemical groups.

problems.what: Gloss a formula symbol (Planck's constant h) used inside a logic expression. It is unclear whether NOTE may follow a « » item inside a function slot.
